title: Theoretical Studies on the Quantitative Structure-Toxicity Relationship of Polychlorinated Biphenyl Congeners Reveal High Affinity Binding to Multiple Human Nuclear Receptors.
authors: Carrera, Andrei Raphael M; Eleazar, Elisa G; Caparanga, Alvin R; Tayo, Lemmuel L
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过QSTR、分子对接和动力学模拟探究多氯联苯与核受体（转录因子家族）的结合亲和力，虽涉及蛋白-配体互作和物理模拟方法，但对象为小分子污染物而非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制研究关联较弱。
abstract: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are organic chemicals consisting of a biphenyl structure substituted with one to ten chlorine atoms, with 209 congeners depending on the number and position of the chlorine atoms. PCBs are widely known to be endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) and have been found to be involved in several diseases/disorders. This study takes various molecular descriptors of these PCBs (e.g., molecular weight) and toxicity endpoints as molecular activities, investigating the possibility of correlations via the quantitative structure-toxicity relationship (QSTR). This study then focuses on molecular docking and dynamics to investigate the docking behavior of the strongest-binding PCBs to nuclear receptors and compares these to the docking behavior of their natural ligands. Nuclear receptors are a family of transcription factors activated by steroid hormones, and they have been investigated to consider the impact of PCBs on humans in this context. It has been observed that the docking affinity of PCBs is comparable to that of the natural ligands, but they are inferior in terms of stability and interacting forces, as shown by the RMSD and total energy values. However, it is noted that most nuclear receptors respond to PCBs similarly to how they respond to their natural ligands-as shown in the RMSF plots-the most similar of which are seen in the ER, THR-beta, and RAR-alpha. However, this study is performed purely in silico and will need experimental verification for validation.
abstract_zh: 多氯联苯（PCBs）是由联苯结构取代一至十个氯原子构成的有机化学品，根据氯原子的数量和位置共有209种同系物。PCBs被广泛认为是内分泌干扰化学物质（EDCs），并已被发现与多种疾病/紊乱相关。本研究采用这些PCBs的各种分子描述符（如分子量）和毒性终点作为分子活性，通过定量结构-毒性关系（QSTR）探讨其相关性的可能性。随后，本研究聚焦于分子对接和动力学，以研究结合力最强的PCBs与核受体的对接行为，并将其与天然配体的对接行为进行比较。核受体是一类由类固醇激素激活的转录因子家族，本研究在此背景下探讨了PCBs对人类的影响。观察到PCBs的对接亲和力与天然配体相当，但在稳定性和相互作用力方面表现较差，这由RMSD和总能量值所示。然而，值得注意的是，大多数核受体对PCBs的响应方式与其对天然配体的响应相似——如RMSF图所示——其中最为相似的是ER、THR-beta和RAR-alpha。然而，本研究纯属计算机模拟，需实验验证以确认其有效性。
